archetype: Mardu vampire typal go-wide aggro with an each-opponent drain sub-engine and a tutorable two-card infinite as a lategame knockout — the engine runs from the command zone via eminence, not from the commander.

role_assignment.default_role: Beatdown. Four-player games trend long and inevitability compounds toward engines (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock), and this deck's late game is a 4.9%-by-t10 natural infinite plus commander-attack triggers — it does not own the long game against dedicated engines, so it must compress the game. Role is seat-relative: against a faster aggro seat it takes the control role behind lords, first strike (Stromkirk Captain), and deathtouch bodies (strategy:whos-the-beatdown).
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: Two concrete pivots. (1) Casting Edgar: goldfish median cast is turn 6 (52.1% by t6), and his attack trigger (+1/+1 counter on each Vampire) converts an accumulated token board into an alpha strike — cast him the turn you intend to swing wide with protection held, not merely on curve (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window). (2) Drawing/tutoring the Vito half onto an established gain-on-loss piece flips the deck from combat clock to a stack-based table-kill attempt; assume every held answer appears the moment you present it.

gameplan_by_phase.early_t1_t3: Deploy cheap Vampires on the 8/19/19 one-two-three curve; every cast banks an eminence token, and a lord or payoff is drawn by t6 in 67.7% of games (mean draw turn 2.7). Do NOT cast Edgar early — the engine costs nothing while he sits in the command zone (strategy:deckbuilding.curve). Mulligan on the engine-deck test: cheap Vampire spells are the enablers, lords/drains the payoffs — enabler-heavy keeps beat payoff-heavy ones (strategy:mulligans.engine-hands).
gameplan_by_phase.mid_t4_t6: Layer amplifiers (doubler drawn 42.4% by t6) and drain pieces (62.5%); Grave Pact turns token deaths into table-wide edicts. Deploy in waves under wrath-math: commit exactly what wins before the near-certain sweeper, hold Bloodghast and hand threats as the rebuild package — eminence itself is the cheapest rebuilder in the format, one token per cast with no recast tax (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math). Manage perceived threat: tokens accrue visibly, so the deflection budget spends down fast (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection).
gameplan_by_phase.late_t7_plus: Take the pivot window: cast Edgar (median t6.6) into a protected alpha strike — his attack trigger pumps every Vampire, Akroma's Will/Boros Charm/Flawless Maneuver cover the swing (protection held 57.1% by t6 in goldfish) — or convert an established gain-on-loss piece into the Vito knockout via Demonic/Vampiric Tutor/Diabolic Intent. Sequence the scariest piece last and count the table's open mana before committing (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window).

key_tensions: Free protection vs the eminence plan: Deflecting Swat and Flawless Maneuver are free only 'if you control a commander' (oracle text) — but the deck's engine works precisely by leaving Edgar in the command zone until t6+. Before Edgar resolves, the protection suite costs real mana (Boros Charm, Teferi's Protection), pinching the same turns the curve wants for casting Vampires (strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance).

Go-wide combat vs ~120 combined life: incremental combat damage is a losing plan against three defenses; the deck's honest answers are the each-opponent drains (Sanctum Seeker, Bloodletter) and the Edgar alpha strike, which is why those pieces, not the lords, are the cards to protect (strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry).

Telegraphed threat vs deflection: eminence tokens from turn 1 make 'I haven't done anything' unsellable — the table's assessment updates every cast, so this deck buys pressure with its deflection budget early and must plan the pivot before the budget is gone (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection).

The infinite is a knockout, not plan A: natural assembly is 2.8% by t6 / 4.9% by t10 (goldfish), but three unrestricted tutors (Demonic, Vampiric, Diabolic Intent — unmodeled by goldfish) and the bracket-4 floor mean opponents will play against it anyway; expect drain-half removal on sight (strategy:deckbuilding.power-level.barometers).

Wrath exposure vs commitment: 29 threat bodies plus tokens against a near-certain sweeper per game; own sweepers are asymmetric (Olivia's Wrath -X/-X to non-Vampires) or life-priced (Toxic Deluge). Commit as much as wins, no further; redeploy worst-first after (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math).

Velocity vs taxes: the 19+19 two/three-drop core is exactly the many-cheap-spells profile that Sphere/Thalia taxes halve — under an assembling lock this deck is forced beatdown, racing the lock's completion (strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial).

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: Assume the wrath; deploy in waves and let eminence be the rebuild — every post-wrath Vampire cast re-banks a token without recasting anything. Hold one protection spell for the committed turn, not after; against control, holding back the whole board IS the loss because buying time is their plan (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math).
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Forced beatdown: taxes halve the two-spell turns this curve is built on, so race the lock's assembly, name the out that breaks the piece that beats YOU (Despark/Fracture/Rite of Oblivion), and remember one stax piece is an inconvenience — the layered second and third are the lock (strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial).
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: Take the control seat of the two-player subgame: lords plus Stromkirk Captain's first strike and Gifted Aetherborn's deathtouch win fair combat, and every drain trigger is life the racer must re-earn. Spend life freely above the threshold where it buys tempo, and keep watching the other two seats — you cannot race three life totals (strategy:combat-math.racing).
matchup_frames.vs_combo: Your combat clock rarely beats a tuned combo turn, so answer economy inverts: against combo the last profitable moment for held interaction is now, not later. Deflecting Swat (once Edgar is out) and the white removal are the cards that matter; your own tutored Vito line is the counter-clock (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy).

distribution_notes: 34 lands but 16 enter tapped — a real tempo tax on an aggro curve; goldfish land-drop rate falls to 59.2% by t6 with only 3 rocks and 1 ritual, and mean available mana is 5.36 on t6 (why Edgar's mean cast is 6.61). Curve is aggressively modal at 2-3 (19+19 of 63 nonland spells, 8 one-drops, 2 spells above MV 5) — on-template per strategy:deckbuilding.curve's hit-2-4-6 discipline. Pips are B-dominant (49 total B pips, source target 36 vs 13 B lands plus fixing/Urborg). Roles: 29 threat bodies vs 10 spot/edict/damage removal and 1 sweeper — a threat-dense, answer-light list that leans on the table per strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry. Caveats: synergy_graph has 0 intra-deck edges (it is a global top-10 shortlist, not a fit score — deck-facts notes), and 12 cards including Exquisite Blood, Grave Pact, and Anointed Procession have no role-taxonomy entry despite being engine pieces.
overall_assessment: This deck plays the game strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry says pure aggro cannot: it is the beatdown (strategy:whos-the-beatdown) whose damage scales to three opponents by construction — wide token boards from a zero-mana command-zone engine, each-opponent drains and edicts instead of single-target damage, and an alpha-strike commander held back as the pivot rather than the plan. Its game is a race against the table's compounding inevitability (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock): spend turns 1-5 converting cheap Vampire casts into a doubled, counter-laden board while managing a rapidly-depleting deflection budget, then take one decisive pivot window — Edgar plus protection for lethal-wide, or a tutor for the Vito half onto a gain engine already in play. The infinites are insurance against the game going long (3% natural by t6, but 3 tutors and a bracket-4 floor make them table-relevant), not the spine; the spine is that every wrath answer the table holds trades against an engine that rebuilds for the cost of casting the next two-drop.
